 THIS CRP FILED UNDER SEC.115 OF CPC., PRAYING TO SET ASIDE THE ORDER DATED 05.08.2023 PASSED ON IA NO.III IN OS NO.605/2022 ON THE FILE OF PRINCIPAL CIVIL JUDGE AND JMFC.,
DEVANAHALLI, THIS REVISION PETITION BE ALLOWED IN THE ENDS OF JUSTICE.

THIS CRP, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER 1.

The petitioners are before this Court seeking for the following reliefs:
" Set-aside the Order dated 05.08.2023 on I.A.No.III in O.S.No.605/2022 passed by the learned Prl. Senior Civil Judge and JMFC., at Devanahalli, this revision petition be allowed in the ends of justice."

2. The respondent No.1 filed a Suit in O.S. No.605/2022 seeking for the following reliefs:
a. To Grant Specific performance of contract that to permit the plaintiff to receive the entire compensation amount in respect of item Nos. 1 & 2 of schedule properties from the 3rd defendant's-KIADB authority b. To grant any other such order as deems fit under the facts & circumstances of the above suit, in the interest of justice and equity.

In the said suit, the petitioner who was defendant No.1 filed an application under Order 7 Rule 11(d) of the Code of Civil Procedure seeking for the following reliefs:
Under Order 7 Rule 11(d) r/w sections 151 of CPC the defendants No.1 and 2 pray that for the reasons sworn to in the accompanying affidavit this Hon'ble Court be pleased to reject the plaint in the ends of justice and equity.
Sri Dalappa vs H P Devaraju on 10 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65608013/
2 4.

entities.text: Sri Dalappa vs H P Devaraju
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The contention of defendant No.1 in the said application is that the property has been granted to the father of defendant No.1 and there is a prohibitory non-alienation period of 15 years in view of the coming into force of the Karnataka Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prohibition of Transfer of Certain Lands) Act, 1979, as such a suit for specific performance of the said agreement without the permission being received from the Deputy Commissioner is not maintainable.

entities.text: Karnataka Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prohibition of Transfer of Certain Lands) Act, 1979
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
Secondly, it was contended that there is a notification which has been issued for acquisition and as such a suit for specific performance is not maintainable and thirdly, it was contended that the agreement of sale which has been relied upon by the plaintiff is a fabricated and forged document which can confirm no title on the plaintiff nor NC: 2024:KHC:21182 can the plaintiff get a right under a forged document seeking for specific performance.
5.

The said application having been objected, the trial Court vide its impugned order dated 5.08.2023 dismissed the said application claiming that filing of a suit for specific performance is not barred.
The agreement of sale was executed on 9.11.2009 and 30.09.2021 was beyond the period of 15 years.

6. A perusal of the said order does not indicate any contention taken by the defendant as regards the requirement of permission being obtained from the Deputy Commissioner for filing a suit for specific performance.

Be that as it may, the suit for specific performance having been filed post the completion of the prohibition period, the aspect of whether the agreement of sale was forged or fabricated, whether such an agreement could have been executed, whether a suit which had been filed in the year 2022 is barred by limitation would have to be ascertained after trial since there is no time period fixed under the agreement of sale NC: 2024:KHC:21182 for execution of the sale deed and there has been no refusal for execution of sale deed prior to filing of a suit.

7. In that view of the matter, I am of the considered opinion that none of the grounds which have been sought to be made out by the plaintiff for rejection of the plaint would in fact satisfy the requirement of Order 7 Rule 11 of CPC requiring the rejection of plaint.
8.

The contentions which have been raised are disputed questions of fact and law and would have to be considered by the trial court after issues are framed, if necessary, by treating the issue as preliminary issue so as to not to delay the proceedings.
9. With the above observation, the petition stands dismissed.
